answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through graph-theoretic trust routing. Honest seeds form a sturdy cedar root, while peer interactions extend along flexible willow branches of transitive credit. Because sparse cuts limit flow into unverified subgraphs, the network denies synthetic swarms a haven, forcing attackers to expend scarce social capital and transaction fees per incoming trust edge. However, this penalizes honest newcomers with high cold-start friction.
